lock_profiling.contention_analysis: Under cross-process execution, namespace_write_lock uses advisory file locking. The lock wraps the entire learn() pipeline (deduplication query + SQLite transaction + audit log). When process A holds the file lock, process B immediately encounters a lock collision (PermissionError [Errno 13] on Windows) and enters an exponential backoff loop with 5-50ms sleep intervals. Under 10 competing processes, backoff sleep accumulates to ~85% of total elapsed time, reducing throughput from 115.9 writes/s (in-process threads) to 2.7-3.3 writes/s (separate OS processes).
lock_profiling.remediation_proposal:
Concrete Architectural Proposal for Multi-Process Concurrency (Scheduled for Future Release):
1. Granular Lock Scope: Narrow namespace_write_lock to protect ONLY the SQLite write transaction    (BEGIN IMMEDIATE ... COMMIT), moving the read-only vector deduplication query outside the critical section.
2. SQLite Native Concurrency: Set PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000 in WAL mode to allow SQLite's internal    page-level lock manager to handle write queueing instead of gross file-level locks.
3. Randomized Micro-Jitter: Replace coarse 5-50ms backoff with randomized microsecond jitter (500us - 2ms)    to prevent lock convoy formation on Windows.
